object.title: The zero-sum 3-flow conjecture for Steiner triple systems
object.statement:
A **Steiner triple system** ${\rm STS}(v)$ is a $2$-$(v,3,1)$ design. A **zero-sum $n$-flow** of a design $\mathcal{D}=(X,\mathcal{B})$ is a map

$$
f:\mathcal{B}\longrightarrow \{\pm1,\ldots,\pm(n-1)\}
$$

such that the sum of the values over all blocks incident with each point is zero. **The zero-sum 3-flow conjecture.** Every ${\rm STS}(v)$ with $v>7$ admits a zero-sum $3$-flow. This conjecture concerns the existence of bounded integer flows on the incidence structures of Steiner triple systems; the source gives no evidence of resolution.
object.source_name: Saieed Akbari, Hamid Reza Maimani, Leila Parsaei Majd and Ian M. Wanless, “Zero-sum flows for Steiner systems”, arXiv:2101.00867 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.00867

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2021).

object.title: The hypoenergeticity conjecture for group-annihilator graphs of cyclic prime-power groups
object.statement: Let $p$ be a prime and let $\alpha$ be a positive integer. Consider the group-annihilator graph realised by the group $\mathbb{Z}/p^{\alpha}\mathbb{Z}$. **Hypoenergeticity conjecture.** For any positive integer $\alpha$, this graph is not hyperenergetic but hypoenergetic. This conjecture extends the preceding result for $\alpha=2$ to all positive integers and concerns the energy of threshold graphs arising from finite abelian groups.
object.source_name: Eshita Mazumdar and Rameez Raja, “Group-annihilator graphs realised by finite abelian groups and its properties”, arXiv:2101.02059 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.02059

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2021).

object.title: The circumference conjecture for essentially 4-connected planar graphs
object.statement:
Let $G$ be an essentially $4$-connected planar graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\operatorname{circ}(G)$ denote the length of a longest cycle in $G$. **Circumference conjecture.** Every essentially $4$-connected planar graph on $n$ vertices satisfies

$$
\operatorname{circ}(G)\ge \frac{2}{3}(n+4).
$$

The bound is motivated by constructions of essentially $4$-connected maximal planar graphs attaining equality. The source states that it remains open whether an essentially $4$-connected planar graph can have smaller circumference; the paper proves the bound for essentially $4$-connected maximal planar graphs.
object.source_name: Igor Fabrici, Jochen Harant, Samuel Mohr and Jens M. Schmidt, “Circumference of essentially 4-connected planar triangulations”, arXiv:2101.03802 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.03802

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2021).

object.title: The stronger $s$-Cohen–Macaulay $M$-vector conjecture
object.statement:
Let $s$ be a positive integer, and let $\Delta$ be an $s$-Cohen–Macaulay complex of dimension $d-1$, with $h$-vector $(h_0,h_1,\ldots,h_d)$. **The stronger $s$-Cohen–Macaulay $M$-vector conjecture.** The vector

$$
(h_0,\ h_1-h_0,\ \ldots,\ h_{\lceil\frac{d+s}{2}\rceil}-h_{\lceil\frac{d+s}{2}\rceil-1})
$$

is an $M$-vector. This would strengthen the usual $g$-theorem-type conclusion for Cohen–Macaulay complexes, but the approach described in the paper gives no clue how to prove the asserted injection or this formulation.
object.source_name: Karim Adiprasito, Stavros Argyrios Papadakis and Vasiliki Petrotou, “Anisotropy, biased pairings, and the Lefschetz property for pseudomanifolds and cycles”, arXiv:2101.07245 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.07245

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2021). “It is equally an open problem to extend the anisotropy to general characteristic.”

object.title: Bounds for the degree-zero chromatic symmetric homology span
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges, let $b$ be the number of blocks of $G$, and let $span_0(G)$ denote the homological span of its degree-$0$ chromatic symmetric homology.

**Span bounds conjecture.** The homological span satisfies

$$
n-b \leq span_0(G) \leq n-1.
$$

The upper bound is proved later in the source, while the lower bound remains part of the conjectural statement from earlier work. Thus the full two-sided conjecture is not resolved by the displayed result.
object.source_name: Azzurra Ciliberti, “A deletion-contraction long exact sequence for chromatic symmetric homology”, arXiv:2211.00699 (2023).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.00699

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2022).

object.title: Shifted Grothendieck positivity conjecture for skew products
object.statement:
Let $\beta$ be the parameter, and let $\boldsymbol{\lambda}$ and $\boldsymbol{\mu}$ be strict partitions. Let $GQ^{(\beta)}_{\lambda/\!/\mu}$ denote the corresponding skew shifted Grothendieck function, and let $\mathbf{GQ}^+$ and $\mathbf{gp}^+$ be the indicated positive spans of shifted Grothendieck functions.

**Shifted Grothendieck positivity conjecture.** One has

$$
GQ^{(\beta)}_{\lambda/\!/\mu} \in \mathbf{GQ}^+
$$

and

$$
gp^{(\beta)}_{\lambda}gp^{(\beta)}_{\mu} \in \mathbf{gp}^+.
$$

These are conjectural positivity properties analogous to the known positivity of products of the corresponding $GP^{(\beta)}$ and $GQ^{(\beta)}$ functions.
object.source_name: Eric Marberg, “Shifted combinatorial Hopf algebras from K-theory”, arXiv:2211.01092 (2023).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.01092

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2022).

object.title: Equivalence of FO- and FOM-transductions
object.statement:
Let 
$$
scr C$ and
$$
scr D$ be infinite classes of finite graphs. An **FO-transduction** interprets graphs using first-order formulas, while an **FOM-transduction** allows first-order formulas with modular counting. **The FO–FOM transduction conjecture.**

$$
\mathscr D \text{ is an FOM-transduction of } \mathscr C \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \mathscr D \text{ is an FO-transduction of } \mathscr C.
$$

The conjecture asks whether modular counting increases the power of first-order transductions on infinite classes of finite graphs. The paper presents this as an unresolved question arising from the fact that it is not clear whether FOM-transductions are more powerful than FO-transductions in general.
object.source_name: J. Nesetril, P. Ossona de Mendez and S. Siebertz, “Modulo-Counting First-Order Logic on Bounded Expansion Classes”, arXiv:2211.03704 (2023).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.03704

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2022).

object.title: Polynomial-move conjecture for enlarging regular polygons in the grasshopper game
object.statement: Let $N>6$ and consider a configuration of grasshoppers at the vertices of a regular $N$-gon, with legal moves given by the grasshopper-jumping game described in the paper. **Polynomial-move conjecture.** Every regular $N$-gon can be transformed to a similar but larger configuration in polynomially many moves in $N$. The main theorem establishes that a finite sequence of moves always exists, while the conjecture asks for a polynomial bound; the explicit bound obtained from the proof is unreasonably large and may be exponential.
object.source_name: János Pach and Gábor Tardos, “Where have all the grasshoppers gone?”, arXiv:2211.03870 (2023).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.03870

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2022).

object.title: Diagram-positivity conjecture for noncommutative monomial symmetric functions
object.statement:
Let $I_H$ be the $H$-graph ideal, and let $\mathfrak{m}_\lambda$ be the corresponding noncommutative monomial symmetric-function element. Say that an element is **diagram positive modulo $I_H$** if its class modulo $I_H$ is a positive sum of arrow diagrams. **Diagram-positivity conjecture.** The elements

$$
\mathfrak{m}_\lambda
$$

are diagram positive modulo $I_H$. The source presents this as an equivalent formulation of the preceding monomial-positivity conjecture, and gives no resolution status.
object.source_name: Jonah Blasiak, Holden Eriksson, Pavlo Pylyavskyy and Isaiah Siegl, “Noncommutative Schur functions for posets”, arXiv:2211.03967 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.03967

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of November 2022). “This conjecture was proven several years later by Brosnan and Chow and independently by Guay-Paquet .”

object.title: Algorithmic Lyubeznik–Barile–Macchia conjecture
object.statement: Let $I$ be a monomial ideal, let $\mathcal{F}_L$ be a Lyubeznik resolution, and let Algorithm $1$ be the trimming algorithm defined in the source. The resulting complex is compared with Barile–Macchia resolutions. **Algorithmic Lyubeznik–Barile–Macchia conjecture.** Applying Algorithm $1$ to a Lyubeznik resolution produces a Barile–Macchia resolution up to isomorphisms. The conjecture would explain why the algorithm systematically yields the rank inequality from the preceding conjecture and would extend the constructions known for certain edge ideals; the source gives this as an open direction rather than a proved result.
object.source_name: Trung Chau and Selvi Kara, “Barile-Macchia resolutions”, arXiv:2211.04640 (2023).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.04640

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2022).

object.title: NP-completeness of maximal non-attacking queen domination on convex polyominoes
object.statement:
A **polyomino** is a finite union of edge-connected unit squares in the plane. It is **convex** if every row and every column has at most one connected component. A set of queens is **non-attacking** when no two queens attack each other, and the maximal domination problem asks whether such a set dominates the polyomino.

**Convex-polyomino maximal queen domination conjecture.** The maximal domination problem for non-attacking queens on convex polyominoes is NP-complete.

The corresponding maximal non-attacking rook problem is known to be in P, but the queen problem has not been settled. The paper notes that existing gadgets are non-convex and leaves this conjecture open.
object.source_name: Alexis Langlois-Rémillard, Mia Müßig and Érika Róldan, “Complexity of chess domination problems”, arXiv:2211.05651 (2025).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.05651

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2022).

object.title: The density domination exponent conjecture for complete bipartite graphs
object.statement:
Let $a_1\ge a_2$ and $b_1\ge b_2$ be positive integers satisfying

$$
a_2\ge b_2>1,\qquad a_1\le b_1,\qquad b_1+b_2\ge a_1+a_2.
$$

For graphs $G$ and $H$, let $\rho(G,H)$ denote the density domination exponent. In particular, write $K_{a_1,a_2}$ and $K_{b_1,b_2}$ for complete bipartite graphs.

**The density domination exponent conjecture.**

$$
\rho(K_{a_1,a_2},K_{b_1,b_2})=\max\left\{\frac{b_1b_2}{a_1a_2},\frac{b_1+b_2-1}{a_1+a_2-1}\right\}.
$$

This conjecture gives the missing case in the paper's determination of density domination exponents for complete bipartite graphs. The supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.
object.source_name: Cynthia Stoner, “The Graph Density Domination Exponent”, arXiv:2211.09870 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.09870

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2022).

object.title: The quarter-size upper-bound conjecture for crossing families of elbows
object.statement: Let $S$ be a set of $n$ points in the plane in general position. An **elbow** is an orthogonal geometric-graph edge consisting of one horizontal and one vertical line segment, and a crossing family of elbows is a family in which every two elbows cross. **Elbow crossing-family conjecture.** There are point sets of $n$ elements that do not admit a crossing family of elbows with more than $\lfloor n/4\rfloor$ elements. The proved lower bound is $\lfloor n/4\rfloor$, while the matching upper-bound construction remains conjectural.
object.source_name: José Luis Álvarez-Rebollar, Jorge Cravioto-Lagos, Nestaly Marín, Oriol Solé-Pi and Jorge Urrutia, “Crossing and intersecting families of geometric graphs on point sets”, arXiv:2211.09904 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.09904

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2022). “It remains as an open problem to close the gap between these bounds. We point out that if Aronov et al.”

object.title: The quadratic upper-bound conjecture for intersecting triangles
object.statement: Let $S$ be a point set with $3n$ elements in the plane in general position. An **intersecting edge-disjoint triangle family** is a family of edge-disjoint triangles such that every two triangles have intersecting edges. **Intersecting-triangle upper-bound conjecture.** Every such point set has at most $n^2$ intersecting edge-disjoint triangles. The paper proves that $n^2$ triangles can be attained for point sets in convex position, so the conjecture asserts that this construction is extremal; it remains open in general.
object.source_name: José Luis Álvarez-Rebollar, Jorge Cravioto-Lagos, Nestaly Marín, Oriol Solé-Pi and Jorge Urrutia, “Crossing and intersecting families of geometric graphs on point sets”, arXiv:2211.09904 (2022).

object.title: The scale-free conjecture for infinity-PageRank
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with vertex set $V(G)$, and let $d_i$ be the degree of node $i\in V(G)$. Suppose

$$
d_i\sim X,
$$

where $X$ is a regularly varying random variable. Let $PR_\infty(i)$ denote the infinity-PageRank value of node $i$.

**Scale-free infinity-PageRank conjecture.** If $d_i\sim X$ where $X$ is a regularly varying random variable, then $PR_\infty(i)$ will also be scale-free.

The conjecture concerns the transfer of heavy-tailed, regularly varying degree behavior to infinity-PageRank values. The source motivates it by similarity with known behavior of standard PageRank, but provides no proof or resolution.
object.source_name: Cory Glover, Tyler Jones, Mark Kempton and Alice Oveson, “Effects of Backtracking on PageRank”, arXiv:2211.13353 (2026).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.13353

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2022).

object.title: The quadratic-orthomorphism cycle conjecture for primes
object.statement:
For a prime $p$ with $p\equiv 1\bmod 8$ or $p\equiv 3\bmod 8$, let $f_p$ be the quadratic orthomorphism over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ used to define the permutation

$$
\phi_p=f_p^{-1}\cdot\tau_p^{-1}\cdot f_p\cdot\tau_p.
$$

Here $\tau_p$ is the cyclic permutation associated with translation on $\mathbb{Z}_p$.

**The cycle conjecture.** For any prime $p\equiv 1\bmod 8$ or $p\equiv 3\bmod 8$, the permutation $\phi_p$ is a $p$-cycle.

The conjecture is presented as an earlier conjecture that the paper aims to prove using link relation matrices. The source does not explicitly state the resolution status of this candidate.
object.source_name: Jack Allsop and Ian M. Wanless, “Row-Hamiltonian Latin squares and Falconer varieties”, arXiv:2211.13826 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.13826

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2022).

object.title: Kinnersley–West–Zamani 3/5-conjecture for the domination game
object.statement:
Let $G$ be an isolate-free graph of order $n$, and let $\gamma_g(G)$ denote the game domination number, the number of vertices selected when Dominator starts and both players play optimally. **Kinnersley–West–Zamani's 3/5-conjecture.** One should have

$$
\gamma_g(G) \leq \frac{3}{5}n.
$$

The source mentions this as a central conjecture for the ordinary domination game, posed by Kinnersley, West and Zamani; the supplied text gives no resolution status.
object.source_name: Julien Portier and Leo Versteegen, “A proof of the 3/4 conjecture for the total domination game”, arXiv:2211.16432 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.16432

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2022).

object.title: Stable transduction conjecture for hereditary graph classes
object.statement:
Let $\mathscr C$ be a hereditary class of graphs. A class is **stable** if no transduction of it contains all finite half-graphs, and it is **nowhere dense** in the standard sparse graph-theoretic sense. A **transduction** is a first-order interpretation operation between classes of structures.

**Stable transduction conjecture.** A hereditary class of graphs is stable if and only if it is a transduction of a nowhere dense class of graphs.

The conjecture seeks a normal form for stable hereditary classes in terms of sparse classes. The supplied text says that it has been proposed as a characterization and gives no evidence of resolution.
object.source_name: Hector Buffière and Patrice Ossona de Mendez, “Decomposing graphs into stable and ordered parts”, arXiv:2505.00594 (2025).
object.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2022–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2204.00722](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.00722).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.00594

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2025).

object.title: Athanasiadis–Kalampogia-Evangelinou's real-rootedness conjecture for Bergman-complex h-polynomials
object.statement: Let $\mathrm{M}$ be a matroid, let $\mathcal{L}(\mathrm{M})$ be its lattice of flats, and let $\Delta(\widehat{\mathcal{L}}(\mathrm{M}))$ be the order complex of its proper nonempty flats, also called the Bergman complex. **Athanasiadis–Kalampogia-Evangelinou's conjecture.** The $h$-polynomial of $\Delta(\widehat{\mathcal{L}}(\mathrm{M}))$ has only nonpositive real roots. This is the $h$-polynomial reformulation of the conjectured real-rootedness of the chain polynomial of a geometric lattice; the source gives no resolution.
object.source_name: Basile Coron, Luis Ferroni and Shiyue Li, “Chow polynomials of rank-uniform labeled posets”, arXiv:2511.13819 (2025).
object.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2022–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2508.13810](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.13810), [arXiv:2208.04893](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04893).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.13819

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2025).

object.title: The inversion number of the tournament $Q_n$
object.statement:
Let $Q_n$ be the tournament obtained from the transitive tournament of order $n$ by reversing the arcs of its unique directed Hamiltonian path.

**The $Q_n$ inversion-number conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{inv}(Q_n)=\left\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\right\rfloor.
$$

The source introduces this as the explicit-tournament motivation for Belkhechine et al.'s lower-bound conjecture. The source does not state a resolution.
object.source_name: Guillaume Aubian, Frédéric Havet, Florian Hörsch, Felix Klingelhoefer, Nicolas Nisse, Clément Rambaud and Quentin Vermande, “Problems, proofs, and disproofs on the inversion number”, arXiv:2212.09188 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.09188

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2022).
